explanation.title: Spanish Agreement & Concordance: Making Words Match

sections.subtitle: Gender Agreement: Masculine & Feminine
sections.content:
⚖️ GENDER AGREEMENT

Spanish nouns have gender (masculine/feminine)
Articles, adjectives, pronouns MUST agree

📋 ARTICLES agree with noun gender:

• EL (masculine) / LA (feminine)
→ El libro (the book - masculine)
→ La mesa (the table - feminine)

• UN (a - masculine) / UNA (a - feminine)
→ Un gato (a cat - masculine)
→ Una casa (a house - feminine)

📋 ADJECTIVES agree with noun gender:

• Masculine: often end in -o
• Feminine: change to -a

→ El libro rojo (red book - rojo masculine)
→ La casa roja (red house - roja feminine)

✅ Adjectives ending in -e or consonants often stay same:
→ El coche grande, La casa grande (both grande)

🔄 CHANGES:

• Drop -o, add -a: bueno/buena, nuevo/nueva, pequeño/pequeña
• Add -a to -or: trabajador/trabajadora
• Nationality: español/española, francés/francesa, alemán/alemana

👤 PRONOUNS agree:
→ Él es alto (He is tall - masculine)
→ Ella es alta (She is tall - feminine)

💡 Even inanimate objects have gender:
→ El libro es interesante (book - masculine)
→ La película es interesante (movie - feminine)

sections.subtitle: Number Agreement: Singular & Plural
sections.content:
🔢 NUMBER AGREEMENT

Articles, adjectives, verbs must agree with noun number

📋 ARTICLES:

• EL/LA (singular) → LOS/LAS (plural)
→ El libro → Los libros
→ La casa → Las casas

• UN/UNA (singular) → UNOS/UNAS (plural - 'some')
→ Un gato → Unos gatos
→ Una mesa → Unas mesas

📋 ADJECTIVES:

Add -s if ending in vowel, -es if ending in consonant

→ Libro rojo → Libros rojos
→ Casa grande → Casas grandes
→ Chico joven → Chicos jóvenes

📋 VERBS agree with subject:
→ El niño come (boy eats - singular)
→ Los niños comen (boys eat - plural)

⚠️ Mixed gender groups → masculine plural:
→ Juan y María son altos
(Juan and María are tall - altos masculine plural)

📋 DEMONSTRATIVES agree:
→ Este libro (this book - masc singular)
→ Estos libros (these books - masc plural)
→ Esta casa (this house - fem singular)
→ Estas casas (these houses - fem plural)

📋 POSSESSIVES agree:
→ Mi libro/Mis libros (my book/books)
→ Nuestro amigo/Nuestros amigos (our friend/friends - masc)
→ Nuestra amiga/Nuestras amigas (our friend/friends - fem)

sections.subtitle: Agreement in Compound Tenses with HABER
sections.content:
🔄 COMPOUND TENSES WITH HABER

When using HABER + past participle for perfect tenses:
Participle is INVARIABLE - doesn't change!

✅ PRESENT PERFECT:
→ He comido (I have eaten - masculine speaker)
→ Ella ha comido (She has eaten - SAME form)
→ Hemos comido (We have eaten - SAME form)

Participle 'comido' NEVER changes

→ María ha estudiado (María has studied)
→ Los estudiantes han estudiado (Students have studied)
→ Same 'estudiado' - no change for feminine plural

✅ PLUPERFECT:
→ Había terminado (I/he/she had finished - same for all)
→ Las chicas habían terminado (Girls had finished)
→ Same 'terminado' - no change

✅ FUTURE PERFECT:
→ Habré llegado (I will have arrived - same for everyone)

🎯 THE RULE:
HABER + past participle = NO AGREEMENT

Only HABER conjugates
Participle stays in -o form (technically masc sing, but used for ALL)

⚠️ EXCEPTION:
Passive voice with SER changes participle
(But that's not a compound tense with haber)

💡 Compare:
✅ He visto la película (I have seen movie - haber, no agreement)
vs
✅ La película fue vista (Movie was seen - ser, agrees with película)

sections.subtitle: Agreement with SER, ESTAR, and Passive Voice
sections.content:
⚖️ AGREEMENT WITH SER/ESTAR + ADJECTIVES/PARTICIPLES

Predicate adjective/participle MUST agree with subject

✅ SER + ADJECTIVE:
→ Juan es alto (Juan is tall - masculine)
→ María es alta (María is tall - feminine)
→ Los niños son altos (Boys are tall - masc plural)
→ Las niñas son altas (Girls are tall - fem plural)

✅ ESTAR + ADJECTIVE:
→ La puerta está abierta (Door is open - feminine)
→ Los libros están cerrados (Books are closed - masc plural)

✅ ESTAR + PARTICIPLE (resultant state):
→ La carta está escrita (Letter is written - feminine)
→ Los documentos están firmados (Documents signed - masc plural)

Participle agrees because it functions as adjective

🔄 PASSIVE VOICE WITH SER:

Past participle acts as adjective and MUST agree

→ El libro fue escrito por Cervantes
(Book was written by Cervantes - escrito masc sing agrees with libro)

→ Las cartas fueron escritas por mi madre
(Letters were written by my mother - escritas fem plural agrees with cartas)

💡 Remember the difference:

❌ With HABER = no agreement
→ He escrito la carta (I have written letter - no agreement)

✅ With SER/ESTAR = full agreement
→ La carta está escrita (Letter is written - escrita agrees)

sections.subtitle: Agreement with Collective Nouns
sections.content:
👥 COLLECTIVE NOUNS

Refer to groups but are grammatically SINGULAR

📋 Common collective nouns:
• GENTE (people)
• FAMILIA (family)
• EQUIPO (team)
• GRUPO (group)
• PAREJA (couple)
• MULTITUD (crowd)
• PÚBLICO (audience)

✅ VERB AGREEMENT:

Collective nouns take SINGULAR verbs (even for multiple people)

→ La gente está contenta
(People ARE happy - gente is singular, so está)

→ Mi familia vive en Madrid
(My family lives - vive singular)

→ El equipo ganó el partido
(Team won - ganó singular)

✅ ADJECTIVE AGREEMENT:

Adjectives agree with grammatical gender/number of collective noun
(NOT with the individuals)

→ La gente es simpática
(People are nice - simpática fem sing agrees with gente)

→ El público estuvo silencioso
(Audience was silent - silencioso masc sing agrees with público)

⚠️ EXCEPTION:

Informal speech sometimes uses plural for emphasis on individuals:
→ La gente estaban contentos (less formal)

However, standard grammar requires singular:
→ La gente estaba contenta ✅

💡 With pronouns referring back:
→ La familia llegó y ellos comieron
(Family arrived and they ate - ellos can refer to members in 2nd clause)

sections.subtitle: Agreement in Complex Sentences
sections.content:
🔗 AGREEMENT IN COMPLEX SENTENCES

1️⃣ RELATIVE CLAUSES

Verbs/adjectives agree with antecedent (noun the pronoun refers to)

→ La chica que vive aquí es simpática
(Girl who lives here is nice - vive agrees with chica singular)

→ Los chicos que estudian mucho son inteligentes
(Boys who study a lot are intelligent - estudian agrees with chicos plural)

→ Busco personas que sean honestas
(Looking for people who are honest - sean plural agrees with personas, honestas plural adjective)

2️⃣ COORDINATION (multiple subjects)

When coordinating subjects with Y (and), verb is plural:

→ Juan y María comen pizza
(Juan and María eat pizza - comen plural)

If genders mixed, adjectives are masculine plural:
→ Juan y María son altos
(altos masc plural - default for mixed)

3️⃣ PARTICIPIAL CLAUSES

Past participle agrees when modifying noun directly:

→ Compré manzanas cultivadas localmente
(I bought apples grown locally - cultivadas fem plural agrees with manzanas)

4️⃣ ABSOLUTE CONSTRUCTIONS

→ Terminada la reunión, nos fuimos
(Meeting finished, we left - terminada agrees with reunión feminine)

5️⃣ QUANTIFIERS

Agreement depends on structure:

→ Mucha gente vino
(Many people came - mucha agrees with gente fem sing, vino singular verb)

→ Muchas personas vinieron
(Many people came - muchas and vinieron plural)

→ La mayoría de estudiantes estudia/estudian
(Most students study - can be singular or plural, both accepted)

questions.question: 'El libro roj___' - Complete with the correct ending.

answers.text: rojo (masculine singular to agree with libro)

questions.hint: Libro is masculine singular, so adjective must be masculine singular: rojo.

questions.question: 'La casa roj___' - Complete with the correct ending.

answers.text: roja (feminine singular to agree with casa)

questions.hint: Casa is feminine singular, so adjective must be feminine singular: roja.

questions.question: 'El chico español, La chica ___' - What's the feminine form?
questions.hint: Nationality adjectives: español (masculine) → española (feminine).

questions.question: 'El profesor trabajador, La profesora ___' - Complete.
questions.hint: Adjectives ending in -or add -a for feminine: trabajador → trabajadora.

questions.question: 'El coche grande, La casa ___' - What form does grande take?
questions.hint: Adjectives ending in -e usually stay the same for both genders: grande.

questions.question: 'Los libros roj___' - Complete for plural.
questions.hint: Libros is masculine plural, so adjective must be masculine plural: rojos.

questions.question: 'Las casas roj___' - Complete for plural.
questions.hint: Casas is feminine plural, so adjective must be feminine plural: rojas.

questions.question: 'Juan y María son ___' (altos/altas) - Which is correct for mixed group?

answers.text: altos (masculine plural for mixed gender groups)

questions.hint: Mixed gender groups use masculine plural: altos (default for groups with both genders).

questions.question: 'He comido' (I have eaten - female speaker) - Should 'comido' change?

answers.text: No - with HABER, past participle never changes
Yes - should be 'comida' for female speaker

questions.hint: HABER + participle = NO AGREEMENT. Past participle is invariable: He comido (all genders/numbers).

questions.question: 'Las chicas han estudiado' - Should 'estudiado' change to 'estudiadas'?

answers.text: No - with HABER, participle stays invariable
Only if using SER instead of HABER

questions.hint: With HABER (han), past participle never changes: han estudiado (same for all).

questions.question: 'María ha visto la película' - Does 'visto' agree with María or película?

answers.text: Neither - with HABER, past participle doesn't agree

questions.hint: HABER = no agreement. 'Visto' stays the same regardless of subject or object.

questions.question: 'Las niñas son alt___' - Complete.
questions.hint: With SER, adjectives agree. Niñas is feminine plural, so altas.

questions.question: 'La puerta está abiert___' - Complete.
questions.hint: With ESTAR, participles/adjectives agree. Puerta is feminine singular: abierta.

questions.question: 'Los documentos están firmad___' - Complete.
questions.hint: With ESTAR, participle agrees. Documentos is masculine plural: firmados.

questions.question: 'Las cartas fueron escrit___ por mi madre' - Complete passive voice.
questions.hint: Passive voice with SER: participle agrees. Cartas is feminine plural: escritas.

questions.question: 'La gente está content___' - Complete. (gente = people)
questions.hint: GENTE (people) is grammatically feminine singular, even though it refers to multiple people: contenta.

questions.question: 'Mi familia vive/viven en Madrid' - Which verb is correct?
questions.hint: Collective nouns like FAMILIA take singular verbs: familia vive (singular).

questions.question: 'El equipo ganó/ganaron el partido' - Which is standard Spanish?
questions.hint: Collective nouns like EQUIPO take singular verbs in standard Spanish: equipo ganó.

questions.question: 'La chica que vive/viven aquí' - Which verb is correct?
questions.hint: In relative clauses, verb agrees with antecedent. Chica (singular) → vive (singular).

questions.question: 'Los chicos que estudia/estudian mucho' - Which verb is correct?
questions.hint: Relative clause verb agrees with antecedent. Chicos (plural) → estudian (plural).

questions.question: 'Juan y María come/comen pizza' - Which is correct?

answers.text: comen (plural - coordinated subjects take plural verb)

questions.hint: Coordinated subjects with Y (and) take plural verbs: Juan y María comen.

questions.question: 'Compré manzanas cultivad___ localmente' - Complete participle.
questions.hint: When participle modifies noun directly, it agrees. Manzanas (feminine plural): cultivadas.

questions.question: 'Terminada la reunión' vs 'Terminado la reunión' - Which is correct?
questions.hint: Absolute construction: participle agrees with noun. Reunión is feminine: Terminada.

questions.question: 'He escrito la carta' vs 'La carta está escrita' - Why different agreement?

answers.text: HABER = no agreement; ESTAR = agreement with subject

questions.hint: HABER + participle = invariable (escrito). ESTAR + participle = agrees (escrita with carta).
